questions.solution:
It is given that i=30°.

The formula for angle of deviation is 
δ=180°-2i

Substituting the values,
δ=180°-60°
=120°

questions.q: For an object placed at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from a lens, a sharp focused image is observed on a screen placed at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the lens. A glass plate of refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and thickness <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is introduced between lens and screen such that the glass plate plane faces parallel to the screen. By what distance should the object be shifted so that a sharp focused image is observed again on the screen?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:
object using the lens formula:
\(\begin{aligned}& \frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v \prime}-\frac{1}{w^{\prime}} \\\Rightarrow & \frac{21}{240} \mathrm{~cm}=\frac{3}{35} \mathrm{~cm}-\frac{1}{u^{\prime}} \\\Rightarrow \frac{1}{u^{\prime}} & =\frac{3}{35} \mathrm{~cm}-\frac{21}{240} \mathrm{~cm} \\\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{u^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{5}\left[\frac{3}{7} \mathrm{~cm}-\frac{21}{48} \mathrm{~cm}\right] \\\Rightarrow \frac{1}{u^{\prime}} & =\frac{1}{5}\left[\frac{144-147}{336}\right] \\\Rightarrow u^{\prime} & =-560 \mathrm{~cm}=-5.6 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}\)
Hence, the object should be at \(5.6 \mathrm{~m}\) in front of the lens.
Hence, the oblect should be moved by 5.6-24= \(3.2 \mathrm{~cm}\).

questions.q: A convex mirror of radius of curvature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> forms an image that is half the size of the object. The object distance is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given R=30 cm

So, f=R2=+15 cm

For convex mirror, virtual image is formed for real object. Thus, magnification m=12

The magnification can be written as

m=-vu   ...1

Equation (1) implies that

12=-vu⇒v=-u2

The relation between the object distance, image distance and the focal length of the mirror is given by

1f=1v+1u   ...2

Equation (2) implies that

115=1-u2+1u=-1u⇒u=-15 cm

questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> in front of a plane mirror. The virtual and erect image is formed by the mirror. Now the mirror is moved by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> towards the stationary object. The distance by which the position of image would be shifted, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: When an object is placed in front of a plane mirror, object distance is equal to the image distance. In the first case, the image distance will be 12 cm from the mirror. In the next case, as the mirror is moved towards the object, the object distance becomes 8 cm. Hence, image distance will also be 8 cm.

questions.q: What is the relative decrease in focal length of a lens for an increase in optical power by 0.1 D from 2.5D ? ['D' stands for dioptre]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & P=\frac{1}{f} \\ & \text { So } P_1=\frac{1}{F_1} \Rightarrow F_1=\frac{1}{2.5} \\ & \text { Next } F_2=\frac{1}{2.6} \\ & \left|\frac{\Delta F}{F_1}\right|=\frac{\left|F_2-F_1\right|}{F_1}=\left|\frac{F_2}{F_1}-1\right| \\ & \Rightarrow\left|\frac{\Delta F}{F_1}\right|=\left|\frac{2.5}{2.6}-1\right|=\frac{0.1}{2.6} \approx 0.04\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
In a medium the speed of light wave decreases to 0.2 times to its speed in free space. The ratio of relative permittivity to the refractive index of the medium is x:1. The value of x is ______.

(Given speed of light in free space =3×108 m s-1 and for the given medium μr=1)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Speed of light in medium is related to speed of light in vacuum c and refractive index μ by v=cμ.

Then, we have μ=cv=c0.2c

⇒μ=5

Refractive index in terms of relative permeability μrand relative permittivityεr  of the medium is stated as μ=ϵr μr

⇒ϵr=μ2μr

∴ ϵrμ=μμr=5

Hence, the value of x=5.
